title: Community
lede: Pyreon is built in the open under the MIT license. Here is where to talk, how to contribute, and where to watch it grow.

items.label: Discord
items.text: Questions, show-and-tell, and talking to the people who build it.

items.label: GitHub
items.text: The code, the issues and every pull request. A star helps other people find it.

items.label: Newsletter
items.text: What shipped, what we measured, what is next. In your inbox.

items.label: Blog
items.text: Long-form posts on how Pyreon works. Full-content RSS at `/blog/rss.xml`.

items.label: Live stats
items.text: Stars, downloads, releases and contributors, refreshed daily.

items.title: Get the repo running
items.text: You need Bun and Node.js. `bun install` also builds every package.
items.code:
git clone https://github.com/pyreon/pyreon.git
cd pyreon
bun install
bun run test

items.title: Branch from main
items.text: Fork the repo and create a feature branch from `main`. Keep commits focused: one logical change each, with an imperative message such as `fix(router): prevent open redirect via sanitizePath`.

items.title: Write the test
items.text: Every change comes with test coverage. Run one package with `bun run --filter='@pyreon/<pkg>' test`.

items.title: Check it
items.text: Run the linters and the typecheck before you push.
items.code:
bun run lint
bun run typecheck

items.title: Add a changeset
items.text: If you touched a published package, describe the change for users. Pyreon is `0.x`: pick `minor` or `patch`, never `major`.

items.title: Open the pull request
items.text: Say what changed and why. CI runs the rest.

items.label: Good first issues
items.text: Issues picked for newcomers. If the list is empty, tell us on Discord what you would like to work on.

items.label: Help wanted
items.text: Issues where extra hands are welcome.

items.label: Contributing guide
items.text: Setup, conventions, the memory-leak checklist and how releases work.

items.title: Search first
items.text: Someone may have hit it already.

items.title: Make it small
items.text: A code snippet, a repo link or a failing test.

items.title: Say where
items.text: Your Bun version, OS and, if relevant, browser.

end.title: Come for the signals. Stay for the changelog.

sources.claim: Stable links /discord, /newsletter, /open (stats refreshed daily); never quote counts
Setup commands, fork and branch from main, tests, lint and typecheck, focused commits, commit message example
Per-package test command; bun install builds packages
Changeset required; minor or patch only
Labels "good first issue" and "help wanted" exist
